newsitem.title: USA: Denver airport revenues exceed expenses.
newsitem.headline: Denver airport revenues exceed expenses.

text.p: The city of Denver said it expects revenues from Denver International Airport to exceed expenses and debt service payments by between $30 million to $40 million for the year ended Dec. 31.
It said the figure is contingent upon final calculation of interest earnings and payment of year-end operating expenses.
The city said the excess amount represents the estimated net revenue that will be used to reduce airlines' operating costs during 1997.
It said operating and maintenance expenditures will be about $6 million less than expected and the airport will incur about $4 million less in debt service due to an "aggressive debt management."
Interest earnings will be "significantly greater" than forecast, it said.
It also said that according to the Federal Aviation Administration, the airport had the lowest percentage of air traffic control delays among the nation's 20 busiest.
